categories.title: Roadmap step
criteria: Implements exactly the ROADMAP.md step named in the pull request title, and ticks its box in the same change
Every behaviour the step describes works through its command (chokepoint-policy, chokepoint-log, chokepoint-init), not only inside a helper
Nothing the step asks for is missing, stubbed or left as a TODO

categories.title: Security posture
criteria: Deny by default holds: nothing the default branch blocks or sends to ask becomes allowed, and a policy or input that does not load still stops the gateway instead of enforcing less
The engine stays a pure function (no network, files or state), and both doors still give the same verdict and rule id for the same call
Credentials and declared hidden context never reach a log, message or report unredacted; new output goes through the existing redaction helpers

categories.title: Correctness
criteria: Exit codes are documented and tested: 0 success, 1 the check failed, 2 the input could not be loaded or read
Every event or file format the change touches validates against the published schema, its version is bumped when its shape changes, and older events still validate
Odd input is handled without a crash: empty, unreadable or huge files, bad encodings, symlinks

categories.title: Tests
criteria: pytest passes, and every new behaviour has a test next to the code it covers
Tests cover bypass attempts, not only the happy path: compound shell commands, case and symlink tricks, edited or reordered input
Every claim the change adds to a README, docs/ or --help output has a test that would fail if the claim became false

categories.title: Code quality and docs
criteria: No new runtime dependency, and it runs on Python 3.10 and 3.14
Matches the code's existing style: small functions, the same naming, no dead code or duplicate helpers
README, INSTALL.md and docs/LIMITATIONS.md change where behaviour or a limit changed
